import Mathlib

open scoped TensorProduct
namespace LatticeSL2
def scalarRing (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q | ∃ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (b : ℚ)⁻¹}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(scalarRing p)
instance (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (scalarRing p).subtype).toAlgebra
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V :=
  Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
def divided {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def ev {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev Ix (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
def Stable {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (a : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, a u ∈ W
def SimpleTriple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Stable W x → Stable W y → Stable W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Preserves {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, a (m : V) ∈ M
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def LiftOf {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, (f m : V) = a (m : V)
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] :
    IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
def L {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V)
def J {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (e : V) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (L p M).comap ((LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ).smulRight e |>.restrictScalars (R p))
def pPart {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) (MR p M) :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (Set.range (fun u : MR p M => (p : ℤ) • u))
abbrev Red {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := ZMod p ⊗[ℤ] MR p M
abbrev RK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  K ⊗[R p] MR p M
abbrev FK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharP K p] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  K ⊗[ZMod p] Red p M
def throughR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (RK κ M) :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  (f.baseChange (R p)).baseChange K
def throughF {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharP K p]
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (FK p K M) :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  (((f.baseChange (R p)).restrictScalars ℤ).baseChange (ZMod p)).baseChange K
def matrixUnit {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    {l : ℤ} (B : Module.Basis (Ix l) F U) (i j : Ix l) : Module.End F U :=
  (B.coord j).smulRight (B i)
def genFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End F U) (b : Ix l → U) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Ix l, x (b i) = if hi : 0 < i.val then
      ((l - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • b ⟨i.val - 1, Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le i.val 1) i.isLt⟩
      else 0) ∧
  (∀ i : Ix l, y (b i) = if hi : i.val + 1 < l.toNat + 1 then
      ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • b ⟨i.val + 1, hi⟩ else 0) ∧
  (∀ i : Ix l, h (b i) = ((l - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def iotaSpec {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V) : Prop :=
  ∀ (r : R p) (m : M), f (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = (algebraMap (R p) ℂ r) • (m : V)
def canonicalR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (C : RK κ M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M) : Prop :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  ∀ (c : K) (r : R p) (m : M),
    C (c ⊗ₜ[R p] (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) = (κ r * c) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m
def pureR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (c : K) (u : MR p M) : RK κ M :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  c ⊗ₜ[R p] u
def canonicalF {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharP K p]
    (κ : R p →+* K) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (D : FK p K M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M) : Prop :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∀ (c : K) (a : ZMod p) (r : R p) (m : M),
    D (c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] (a ⊗ₜ[ℤ] (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m))) =
      ((ZMod.cast a : K) * κ r * c) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m
def basisOrigin {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] {l : ℤ}
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V)
    (β : Module.Basis (Ix l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℂ, b ∈ J p M (ev y v 0) ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧
  ∃ ι : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V, iotaSpec p M ι ∧ Function.Injective ι ∧
  ∃ B : Module.Basis (Ix l) (R p) (MR p M),
    (∀ i, ι (B i) = b • ev y v i.val) ∧
  ∃ κ : R p →+* K, ∃ C : RK κ M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M,
    canonicalR κ M C ∧ ∀ i, β i = C (pureR κ 1 (B i))
end LatticeSL2
open LatticeSL2

source_steps.text: Choose b≠0 in J with J=Rb using N004. The family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R by N004, using iota from N002. Define beta_i to be its reduced image in V_K through F001. Scalar extension of its coordinate maps gives a K-basis: every pure tensor has its finite coordinate expansion in beta_i, and the extended coordinate maps take beta_i to the corresponding coordinate unit vectors, proving independence. Therefore dim_K V_K=|I|=n=λ+1>0 by N001 and H002. Applying N001 to b e_i and using the tensor isomorphisms gives x beta_0=0, x beta_i=(λ−i+1)beta_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<λ, y beta_λ=0; h beta_i=(λ−2i)beta_i. All coefficients are the integer images in K. This proves the required basis and its generator matrices.

Operator sums, compositions and scalar multiplication have these same operations on pure tensors, so preserve identities. This verifies the scalar-extension steps already displayed in S003-S004.

# Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice

## Original exercise

James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
\(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).

> 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
> prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.

## Definitions and complete target

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.

1: # Retained authors, immutable interfaces and proof repair
2: 
3: This protocol is generic. No domain, historical node ID or particular notation
4: activates a repair. Task names below describe responsibilities, not a new ID scheme.
5: 
6: ## Preprocessing author and independent reviewer
7: 
8: The controller verifies actual accepted NL0/A authority, then retains one author
9: through optional shared extraction and interface construction. A no-change decision
10: skips incremental review. A changed source gets actual producer/substitution review
11: by the separate retained preprocessing reviewer. Located failures return to that
12: same author; changed candidates return to that same reviewer. Operational faults
13: pause rather than masquerading as mathematical revision requests.
14: 
15: The reviewer next checks the complete typed contract and plan: every external E
16: and full P including all hypotheses, quantifiers and domains; relevant definitions,
17: structure fields, library parameter/index meanings, coercions and nonvacuity. Read
18: the actual pinned definitions instead of guessing from notation. A well-typed
19: encoding may still strengthen or weaken the source. The reviewer is independent
20: of the author, while retaining its own earlier findings; disclose both facts.
21: 
22: Only a complete actual passing semantic receipt opens freeze and proof dispatch.
23: Freeze source, pins, complete endpoint types and the meaning-determining header.
24: Save the handoff and close both preprocessing roles. An unchanged rejected proposal
25: does not justify repeated reviews. This semantic authority is inherited at final
26: machine acceptance only when the actual final artifact still matches it.
27: 
28: ## Local proof work
29: 
30: Each node has its own retained author. Ordinary compiler/API/tactic feedback stays
31: with that author. A 300-second native timeout or heartbeat failure retains the
32: candidate and supplies frozen ST020 advice in the failed tool result. Isolate the
33: expensive application, repair and recheck the unchanged target. There is no total
34: case, token, call, repair-round or turn allowance by default.
35: 
36: `report_proof_obstruction` records a concrete alleged layer, explanation, resolving
37: packet locations and actual own candidate evidence. An allegation is not a proved
38: interface defect. Preserve healthy siblings and let already active work reach its
39: normal handoff. No fixed count of idle replies retires the round, cancels queued
40: jobs or changes inputs. Progress counters remain passive measurement.
41: 
42: After local assignments reach handoffs, the serial connection author may diagnose
43: a reported global issue using its actual source/formal pair and selected own
44: attempts. It may repair internal proof bodies, proved local helpers, parameter
45: applications, library discharges and proof connections. It cannot change frozen
46: E/P, their hypotheses or definitions determining their meaning. A missing producer
47: cannot become an assumption. Ordinary local repair returns to the owning author.
48: 
49: A located frozen-contract defect, source gap or unresolved mathematical obstruction
50: pauses with saved evidence for the user. No automatic unfreeze, source rewrite,
51: whole-workflow restart or new model/profile is authorized. Repeated identical
52: obligation/evidence after a located advice handoff stays an explicit checkpoint;
53: it is not a reason to resample a diagnostic or declare mathematical impossibility.
54: 
55: ## Assembly and final machine acceptance
56: 
57: Attempt mechanical assembly first. If it fails with an actual connection error,
58: use the connection author under the immutable contract. Recheck the complete
59: standalone file, all internal producer dependencies and actual kernel trust.
60: No `sorry`, undeclared project premise or unproved substitute may remain.
61: 
62: Normal final Audit B checks actual full E/P types by native definitional equality,
63: exact frozen header/pins and bound semantic authority, plus complete proof closure.
64: It calls no final semantic model. Its receipt says `FROZEN_INTERFACE_SEMANTICS_INHERITED`,
65: not that a new independent final review took place. Source qualifications remain.
66: 
67: Only a valid proof with genuine endpoint/meaning drift may open B-final. Missing
68: compilation, changed provenance, missing dependencies or `sorry` cannot use this
69: exception. Actual B-final fidelity PASS permits warning-qualified delivery and
70: records the freeze-integrity defect. A nonpass pauses locally and asks the user:
71: 
72: - `deliver-actual`: deliver the compiled statement and findings, explicitly **not**
73:   completion of the original target.
74: - `recheck`: perform the explicitly requested new detailed semantic review, keeping
75:   earlier findings, costs and its actual review scope in the evidence.
76: - `reset-translation`: release translation processes, remove translation-generated
77:   source/native/temp files, retain original NL0/A and cost ledgers, and rerun only
78:   translation. Report the freeze defect to developers.
79: 
80: These are exact-incident `yui.py final-decision` controls displayed in the offline
81: pause report. None is automatic. A stale incident, changed owner, changed artifact
82: or unconfirmed owned-process cleanup blocks the action. User cancellation remains
83: available. A user acceptance of files never grants fidelity or original-goal PASS.
84: 
85: ## Evidence and lifetimes
86: 
87: A submission is a durable handoff, followed by a confirmed native turn interrupt;
88: its role waits without another provider request. The native thread is reused for
89: that role's next assignment. Only the specified accepted handoff closes a role;
90: a fault preserves the carrier, drafts and diagnostics. Controller-authenticated
91: restoration of an interrupted dynamic-tool result is logged and hash-bound; unknown
92: calls or altered history remain rejected.
93: 
94: Reuse only exact checked contexts. Successful bodies copied between retained proof
95: runs are candidates until current Lean checks accept them. Save rejected drafts,
96: actual retries/waits and all reported usage. Selected proof rounds use bound
97: `proof-selection.json`; retained earlier failures are not free or new successes.
98: Missing usage or actual service tier remains unknown; cached/reasoning tokens are
99: subsets. Owner monitoring is bounded read-only observation and supplies no hints.

value.representation_notes: λ is the integer l; nonnegative exponents are Nat and I is Fin (l.toNat+1), identified with 0≤i≤λ using H002. V is an arbitrary complex module; x,y,h are its linear action endomorphisms. H003 records the sl₂ Chevalley relations, highest weight and complex irreducibility. M is an arbitrary Submodule ℤ V, equivalently an additive subgroup, with the integer/complex basis and divided-power stability in H005. R is the rational subring generated by inverses of integers not divisible by p; T006 proves it is exactly the specified ℤ_(p). Scalar actions use its inclusion R→ℚ→ℂ. MR is the actual R⊗ℤ M; its image L is used only through the checked iota in T006/T008. J is the coefficient submodule defined by membership in L. VK=K⊗ℤ M uses the tensor commutor identification with the source M⊗ℤ K. Operators are the actual scalar extensions of compatible integral endomorphisms; existence is proved, and compatible lifts are unique. Red=ZMod p⊗ℤ MR is identified with MR/pMR by T018, and FK is its extension to K. RK and FK install only canonical scalar actions internally. matrixUnit B i j sends B j to B i and other basis vectors to zero; multiplication of endomorphisms is composition with the right factor acting first. No Audit A note is a premise, verified Lean theorem or instance assumption; the two M declarations are used directly from pinned Mathlib.

import Mathlib

open scoped TensorProduct
namespace LatticeSL2
def scalarRing (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q | ∃ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (b : ℚ)⁻¹}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(scalarRing p)
instance (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (scalarRing p).subtype).toAlgebra
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V :=
  Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
def divided {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def ev {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev Ix (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
def Stable {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (a : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, a u ∈ W
def SimpleTriple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Stable W x → Stable W y → Stable W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Preserves {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, a (m : V) ∈ M
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def LiftOf {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, (f m : V) = a (m : V)
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] :
    IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
def L {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V)
def J {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (e : V) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (L p M).comap ((LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ).smulRight e |>.restrictScalars (R p))
def pPart {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) (MR p M) :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (Set.range (fun u : MR p M => (p : ℤ) • u))

argument.text: The reduction homomorphism R→F_p sends an integer fraction to numerator times inverse denominator. It is surjective because integers already map onto F_p. Its kernel is pR: a reduced fraction maps to zero exactly when its numerator is divisible by p, and division of that numerator by p stays in R. Consequently R/pR≅F_p and M_R/pM_R is an F_p-module.
